title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
This incident shows a failure of trust verification in a cryptocurrency investment workflow. A scammer used an AI-generated fake website to display false account balances and investment gains to a victim, creating the appearance that money was growing when it was not. The deception occurred in the interface layer where a user checks their account, a point where human verification of the counterparty's identity could have prevented loss.

The scam exploited a gradual escalation pattern, beginning with small withdrawals that succeeded to build confidence before larger sums were requested. No mechanism is reported to have verified that the website or app belonged to a legitimate entity, or that the returns shown matched any actual trades. It is not established whether the legitimate trading app itself had weaknesses that enabled the fake website to work, or whether the scammer simply directed users to a separate fraudulent site.

It is not established whether the cryptocurrency exchange, trading app, or any platform involved in this incident was aware of the fake website or whether they had detection systems in place.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a sophisticated cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest through a legitimate-looking mobile trading app, beginning with small amounts that showed modest returns and could be withdrawn. This built trust over time, encouraging larger investments. When Dunaway tried to withdraw more money last week, he discovered the funds were gone. Police determined that while the app was real, scammers had created an AI-generated fake website that showed false account balances and investment gains on his screen.

The couple, Jerry and Mindy Dunaway, are now warning others about the sophisticated tactics used by these criminals. They acknowledge that investigators say victims in such cases rarely recover their money. Their children have started a GoFundMe page to help them with daily expenses as they work with Gwinnett County police. The Dunaways emphasize that scammers are highly skilled at manipulating victims and urge people to remain vigilant when approached with investment opportunities.
